findings.failure_path: Adding time.sleep(60) keeps the immediate parent alive until timeout. Previously that parent exited immediately, leaving the descendant holding inherited stdout. A runtime regression that skips process-group cleanup once the immediate parent has exited can now pass this test, so the repair removes the original edge-case coverage.
findings.smallest_fix: Wait for the descendant readiness file, then let the parent exit. Retain the longer timeout and bounded descendant-termination check.

findings.failure_path: os.kill(pid, 0) succeeds for zombies. When group cancellation kills both processes and the orphaned descendant is not promptly reaped, such as under a container PID 1 that does not reap children, the loop reports it alive and fails despite successful termination. The finally block cannot fix this because SIGKILL does not reap a zombie.
findings.smallest_fix: Distinguish terminated zombies from running descendants, or arrange explicit child ownership and waiting so the test can verify termination and reap the fixture deterministically.

challenge_focus: Fifth delta pass: two baseline test repairs found by the required local lanes, plus their register row and dispositions. (a) test_eval_runtime.py: the descendant-timeout case had a 0.5 s budget that two interpreter start-ups exceed on a loaded host; it now waits for the descendant pid, uses a 3 s budget, polls the pid, and reaps it in finally. (b) test_opencode_review_retry.sh: timeout cases used a 5 s wrapper budget against an 8 s stub hang; now 15 s against 24 s. Check that each test still fails when the behaviour it protects is broken and that no assertion was weakened. Report any P0/P1 or P2.
